newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: FISCHER EXPECTS HOWARD BACK AT WORK ASAP
The Acting Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, says he expects John Howard to be out of hospital and back at work as soon as possible.
With Mr Howard still in hospital, Mr Fischer has taken over the reins and will chair a Cabinet meeting in Perth tomorrow.
He says Mr Howard is resting and will hopefully return to work soon.
The Acting Prime Minister says the Government is getting on with the task in Mr Howard's absence, and on Radio National he dismissed media speculation about the leadership succession.
"It is the biggest load of garbage I've heard in months and should be regarded as such," he said.
Mr Fischer also defended the decision to have Cabinet travel outside Canberra, saying the Government is determined to get back to the grass roots and explaining Government policy.
"The super news on inflation, the exporters' dollar, the more realistic value for the dollar is some of the things we have delivered," he said.
And Mr Fischer, says the fallout from the publication of Government documents commenting on South Pacific nations and leaders will eventually go away.
Two documents from the recent meeting of South Pacific Economic Ministers found their way into the media, leading to criticism from some of the Pacific leaders named in them.
Mr Fischer says Australia has been in touch with all the Governments involved, and the Government is working through the outcome of the leak in a systematic way.
COMMONWEALTH BANK STAFF BACK INDUSTRIAL CAMPAIGN
Thousands of employees of the Commmonwealth Bank have backed a call for an industrial campaign, if the bank doesn't change its position in enterprise bargaining.
A packed meeting at Sydney Town Hall was relayed by satellite to meetings across the state.
The Finance sector union is seeking a seven per cent pay rise for its members with no trade-offs.
The union says the bank's enterprise agreement offer provides for no pay rise and would cut away working conditions, reduce rostered days off and redundancy provisions.
Speakers from the floor at today's meeting condemned the bank's attitude to both staff and customers.
New South Wales Finance Sector Union Secretary, Peter Presdey, spoke against immediate industrial action.
Instead, a motion passed unanimously has authorised a campaign of industrial action from August 22 if there's no progress.
HANSON RULES OUT RUNNING FOR SENATE
Independent MP Pauline Hanson has ruled out running for the Senate at the next Federal election.
She says she is used to the processes in the Lower House.
Former Labor Premier, Wayne Goss, is seeking pre-selection for the seat of Oxley to Brisbane's west, with proposed boundary changes likely to make it difficult for Hanson to retain the seat.
But Miss Hanson says it's a shame the Electoral Commission proposes to chop her Oxley electorate in half.
She says it'll be tough to decide whether to stand again in Oxley or opt for the new set of Blair.

"I've got half my constituents in Blair and the other half in Oxley. And it's a real shame that they've done this because Ipswich is a city on its own. It's not the backyard to Brisbane. We're very proud up here in Ipswich and it's a big decision for me to make," she said.
Meanwhile, the Acting Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, has expressed support for John Bjelke-Petersen who's considering standing for the proposed seat of Blair.
The new seat, which would incorporate some of the existing seat of Oxley, has been proposed in a draft re-drawing of electoral boundaries.
Mr Fischer, who's also Federal National Party leader, has told Radio National Blair would be the most likely seat for Mr Bjelke-Petersen, the son of former Queensland Premier, Joh Bjelke-Petersen.
FARMERS DISILLUSIONED BY HOWARD GOVERNMENT
A big farm conference in Queensland has been told the Howard Government has lost the faith of the people it claims to represent.

Graingrowers president, Ian Macfarlane, has told 450 delegates at their annual conference in Toowoomba the Federal Coalition is delivering only pain and empty mutterings to the rural voters it once courted.
He repeated the National Farmers Federation's call for an Office of Rural Affairs in the Prime Minister's office.
He questioned the priorities of the Prime Minister's office saying it takes in Womens Affairs and ATSIC.
"If those offices are given the premise of the Prime Minister and Cabinet surely the issue of rural affairs is just as important if not more important," Mr Macfarlane said.
"Rural industry is about taking this economy forward and we need the backing and the shove of the Prime Minister himself."
HIGH SPEED RAIL SYSTEM THROUGH SEVERAL STATES
An Australian company says it will have a high speed railway running from Melbourne to Darwin, through central Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland by 2003
The chairman of The Australian Transport and Energy Corridor Company, Everald Compton, says it will cost $10-billion.
He says it will carry passengers at 300 kilometres an hour and light freight at 200 kilometres an hour, connecting with high speed catamarans running from Darwin to Asian markets.
"There is no trouble getting investors all around the world," Mr Compton said.

"We've done our homework about that. If we can stack the figures up we'll get investors who'll put it on. In fact it's not the money that's the worry, It's getting five Governments to co-operate," he said.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
